Using the OpenRouter model pricing page

The page is a searchable snapshot of every model on OpenRouter, with prices, an estimated cost per task, speeds, benchmark scores and privacy. This guide explains each part of the page.

Quick start

  1. Type a model or provider name in Search, for example claude or gemini flash NOT lite.
  2. Pick a Profile under Task cost that matches your work, such as Coding & Refactor or General Chat. The Task Cost column then shows what one such task costs on each model.
  3. Click a column header to sort, for example Task Cost to put the cheapest models first.
  4. Click a row to see its details, including every provider that hosts the model, with its speed and price.
  5. To keep only private models, open the ZDR tab.
  6. Overwhelmed by choice? Set Feature to ranked models to see only the 60 or so models people use most on OpenRouter.

Page layout

From the top down:

  • Title and snapshot time. The line under the title says when the data was collected, in UTC. Prices are in US dollars, as OpenRouter bills.
  • Tabs: all models, or private models only.
  • Controls: search, Feature, Category, Colour by, the Task cost group (Profile and Effort), Versions, release date, Hide retiring and Speeds.
  • Band chips: one per colour band, to show or hide those rows. The row count is at the right.
  • The model table, one row per model.
  • The footer, which lists the data sources and the band limits.

Tabs

  • All models lists every model in the catalogue.
  • ZDR lists only models with at least one zero-data-retention (ZDR) host, where the provider does not store prompts or outputs. On the published page this tab is called ZDR + no training: the models are also allowed by an API key that enforces both ZDR and no training on your data.

The number on each tab is how many models it holds with the current search and filters.

Search

Words match the model ID, the name and the features. Several words must all match. Click Search help for a summary on the page.

TypeFinds
gemini flashmodels matching both words
claude OR gptmodels matching either word
gemini NOT lite, gemini -liteGemini models without “lite”
"deep research"the exact phrase
(claude OR gpt) NOT miniparentheses group terms; &&, || and !word also work

Number filters

A field, an operator (> >= < <= =) and a number, with no spaces needed. Mix them with words: coding>50 in<1 finds models with a Coding score above 50 and an input price under $1 per million tokens. Money is in US dollars, and k and m work as suffixes (ctx>=200k). A model with no value for a field never matches a filter on it.

FieldColumnCompares
taskcostTask Costestimated cost of one task for the selected profile, USD
inInput / 1Minput price per 1M tokens, USD
outOutput / 1Moutput price per 1M tokens, USD
reasoningReasoning / 1Mseparate reasoning price per 1M tokens, USD
ctxContextcontext window in tokens (200k, 1m)
ttftTTFTtime to first token, seconds
tpstok/sthroughput, tokens per second
codingCodingArtificial Analysis coding index
intelIntelligenceArtificial Analysis intelligence index
agentic—Artificial Analysis agentic index
zdrPrivacynumber of zero-data-retention hosts (0 = none)
privatePrivacy1 = ZDR + no training, else 0
rankUsage rankbest usage rank in any category (1 = most used)

Price filters (in, out, reasoning) only match prices per token, so speech and transcription models priced per hour or per character never match them.

Feature and version filters

  • Feature keeps models that accept or produce a kind of input or output, or, with ranked models, only the models in OpenRouter’s usage rankings (see Usage ranks). The other choices are text, file (documents and PDFs), image in (vision and OCR), image out (generation), audio in (transcription), audio out (speech), video in or out, or embeddings.
  • Versions hides older releases: Newest per family or Newest 2 per family. A family is the model name without its version number, so “Claude Sonnet 5” and “Claude Sonnet 5.5” are one family. Models without a version number are always shown.
  • Release date keeps models released in the last 12 or 24 months.
  • Hide retiring hides models OpenRouter has scheduled for retirement.

When filters hide rows, the count reads, for example, “Showing 120 of 664 ⓘ”. Hover it to see how many rows each filter hides, or click it to clear the search and filters and show every model again.

Usage ranks and categories

OpenRouter ranks the most-used models in each of 12 categories: Academia, Finance, Health, Legal, Marketing, Programming, Roleplay, Science, SEO, Technology, Translation and Trivia. The ranking is by how many tokens OpenRouter users send to each model, about the top 20 per category.

  • Category shows only the models ranked in that category, sorted by rank with #1 (most used) first.
  • The Rank column shows the rank in the chosen category or, with All categories, each model’s best rank in any category. Hover a cell for all its ranks, for example “Programming #10 · Finance #13”. Models ranked in more categories sort first when their best ranks tie.
  • The row details list the ranks too, and the search field rank filters by the best rank, for example rank<=5.
A usage rank measures popularity, not quality. Cheap, fast models often top the rankings because they handle large volumes. To compare quality, sort by Coding or Intelligence; for cost, use Task Cost.

Why the usage rank differs from the Coding score

The usage rank and the Coding score measure different things, so they often disagree:

  • Usage rank counts how many tokens OpenRouter users send to a model: what people use.
  • Coding and Intelligence are Artificial Analysis test scores: how well a model does.

For example, the Programming ranking is often led by fast, low-cost “Flash” models, while models with the highest Coding scores rank lower or not at all. The reasons:

  • Price drives volume. Coding agents, autocomplete and batch jobs send very large numbers of tokens. Models that cost 20 to 100 times less collect most of that traffic, even when they score a few points lower.
  • A few large users can dominate. One busy app can move a model up a ranking on its own.
  • Only OpenRouter traffic counts. Many people use Claude or GPT directly from Anthropic or OpenAI, or through tools such as Claude Code. That use is not in OpenRouter’s counts, so strong models can rank low there.
  • Not every ranked model has a score. New models are often ranked before Artificial Analysis tests them, so their Coding column shows a dash.
  • They change at different speeds. Ranks follow recent traffic; scores change only when a model is tested again.

Use the usage rank to see what other people rely on at scale. To choose a model, compare Coding or Intelligence for quality and Task Cost for cost. For example, the search coding>70 taskcost<0.01 finds strong coders that are also cheap to run.

Colours and band chips

Each row is coloured by a band. Colour by chooses what the band measures:

  • Token price (per 1M): the highest of the input, output and reasoning prices. Free Cheap ≤ $1.00/M Mid ≤ $5.00/M Expensive > $5.00/M Variable routing Unknown
  • Task cost (selected profile): the Task Cost column, with limits that suit each profile (for Coding & Refactor: ≤ $0.005, ≤ $0.02 and > $0.02 per task).

The footer shows the limits in use. Variable routing marks routers such as openrouter/auto, whose price depends on the model chosen for each request. Unknown covers models with no comparable price, including speech and transcription models priced per hour or per character.

The band chips above the table are on/off switches. Click one to hide its rows (it turns white with a dashed border); click again to show them.

Task cost

The Task Cost column estimates what one typical task costs on each model at its current prices. Choose the task with Profile:

  • Coding & Refactor, General Chat, Document / RAG, Deep Reasoning / Math and Autonomous Agent (15 turns), for text work.
  • Vision / Document OCR (1 image), Image Generation (1 image) and Video Analysis (1 min).
  • Audio Transcription (1 min). For transcription models billed by audio length, this is 60 seconds at the model’s rate.

The estimate counts input, output and reasoning tokens, and allows for how many tokens each model’s tokenizer uses for the same text, and for prompt caching. Hover a Task Cost cell for the breakdown.

Effort sets how hard reasoning models think, which changes how many reasoning tokens they bill. Model default uses each model’s own default. A fixed level (None, Minimal, Low, Medium, High, Very high or Max) is matched to the nearest level each model supports.

N/A means the model cannot do that task: for example, a text task on an image model, or a model with no comparable price.

Task costs are estimates for comparing models, not quotes. Real costs depend on your prompts, the answers and how often the cache is reused.

Speeds

The Speed column shows time to first token (TTFT) and output tokens per second (tok/s), from OpenRouter’s statistics for each provider. Speeds chooses which figures to show:

  • Typical (sampled): the median of samples taken every 3 hours over recent days. This is the steadiest figure and the default.
  • Latest 30 min: the 30 minutes before the snapshot, shown as a range from the slowest host to the fastest, for example 0.49s–1.45s.
  • Peak hours and Off-peak hours: the medians during the slowest and fastest times of day. These options appear once a week of samples has been collected.

Hover a speed cell for more detail. A dash means OpenRouter had no recent speed data for that model.

Columns

ColumnShows
ModelThe name in bold, with the model ID to use in the OpenRouter API underneath. A leading ~ marks a “latest” alias that always points to the newest version, and :batch, :free and similar suffixes are variants with their own prices. Sorting by Model sorts by ID.
FeaturesInputs and outputs in short form: img image input, gen generates (img gen, vid gen), aud audio, vid video, stt transcription, tts speech, embed embeddings. Hover a cell for the full list.
ContextThe context window in tokens (1.0M = one million).
In / 1M, Out / 1MInput and output prices per million tokens in US dollars.
Task CostEstimated cost of one task for the selected profile (see Task cost).
SpeedTime to first token · output tokens per second, for example 3.49s · 74 (see Speeds). Sorting by Speed puts the fastest first.
Code, IntelArtificial Analysis coding and intelligence indexes, as published by OpenRouter. Higher is better.
RankOpenRouter’s usage rank (see Usage ranks). A dash means the model is not in any category’s top 20.
🔒Privacy: 🔒 = ZDR + no training, ZDR = a zero-data-retention host only, blank = neither. On a page published without a key check, it shows ZDR or blank.

Hover a column header for a short explanation.

Choosing columns

The table shows the essentials by default so it fits a laptop screen. Columns ▾, at the right above the table, lists every column with a tick box: tick one to show it, untick to hide it. Extra columns you can add:

  • Model ID and Name as separate columns.
  • Reasoning / 1M: the separate reasoning price, where a model has one (otherwise reasoning tokens are billed as output).
  • Band: the row’s colour band in words (see Colours).
  • TTFT and tok/s as separate columns, to sort by time to first token.

Your choice is remembered in this browser and kept in the page link. Reset columns, in the same menu, restores the default columns and order.

Speech and transcription prices

Most speech (text-to-speech) and transcription (speech-to-text) models are not priced per token, so their price cells show the unit from the model’s OpenRouter page instead:

  • Per hour of audio, for example $0.360/hr. Prices billed per second or per minute are converted to per hour, so the column reads in one unit; hover the cell for OpenRouter’s own listing (for example $0.0001/second).
  • Per million characters ($7.00/M chars) or per million bytes ($15.00/M bytes) of text, for speech models.
  • $7.00 units means OpenRouter’s page did not confirm the unit.

These prices are not comparable with token prices, so they are not colour-banded (band unknown) and sort after the token prices, grouped by unit. Some speech models, such as Gemini TTS and GPT-4o Transcribe, are priced per token and appear like any other model.

Sorting and moving columns

  • Sort: click a column header. Click again to reverse the order. The ▲ or ▼ marks the sorted column. Rows without a value go last.
  • Move a column: drag its header left or right; a blue line shows where it will land. This works in desktop browsers, not on phones.
  • Your column order is remembered in this browser. Reset columns, in the Columns ▾ menu, puts the columns back in their default order.

On a phone

On a narrow screen the page shows one card per model instead of the table. Each card shows the name and ID, the prices and Task Cost, and the speed, scores and usage rank, coloured by band like a table row.

  • Tap a card to open its details; tap it again to close them. The providers table scrolls sideways.
  • Sort by chooses the order, and ↑↓ reverses it.
  • Filters opens Feature, Category, Colour by, Task cost, Versions and Speeds. Tap Hide filters to fold them away again.
  • Search, the tabs and the band chips work as on a computer.

Row details

Click a row to open its details below it; click again to close them. The details show:

  • Reasoning effort: the levels the model supports, its default, the level the Task Cost uses, and the request setting to choose a level yourself, for example "reasoning": {"effort": "medium"}.
  • Privacy and ZDR providers: which hosts keep no data, with the endpoint names to use when routing.
  • Prices and the model’s description.
  • Providers: every host of the model, with its speed over the last 30 minutes and its prices.
    • ● and a blue tint mark the hosts whose prices the row uses. With OpenRouter’s default routing, any of the marked hosts may serve your request.
    • ⚡ marks the fastest host, which OpenRouter uses when you add :nitro to the model ID.
  • A link to the model on OpenRouter.

Sharing a view

The page address records your search, tab, filters, category, colours, task profile, sort, and column order and choice. Copy the address from the browser to share exactly what you see; it opens the same view for anyone.

If the page is opened from inside another site, such as SharePoint, the address cannot record the view. Everything else works normally.

Good to know

  • The page is a snapshot. Prices and speeds are as of the time under the title, and the published page is refreshed once a day.
  • OpenRouter bills in US dollars. Some models have extra charges not shown in the table, such as web search or per-image fees; the model’s OpenRouter page lists them.
  • Data comes from the OpenRouter API. Coding and Intelligence are Artificial Analysis indexes, as published by OpenRouter.
  • The page is a single file with no tracking and no outside scripts, so it also works offline once saved.
